One of the objectives for cultivation is to nourishing the body and strengthen the body to attain good health, and calm and tranquil the heart (mind) as discussed. It is better done in a static condition. It is only when one has a strong and healthy body, and calm and tranquil heart (mind) then one is able to diligent and steadfast engaging the body. One of the objectives for training is to applying the body to move correctly as discussed. It is better done in a dynamic condition. The basic requirement for training is a strong and healthy body. Without a strong and healthy body, it is not possible to applying the body with good result. Cultivation and training for martial art are two separating subjects with different emphasis and exercises. They are prioritized into first and second order. Cultivation is first and training is second. Based on the objective, it is possible to substitute first for second, but not possible to substitute second for first to attain good result. Therefore, the correct order for martial art training is first one should engage in cultivation exercise to develop a strong and healthy body and later engage in training exercise to achieve skill and profundity. If one is following in this order, the martial art training is successful, so the body is healthy and the skill is excellent. Otherwise, it is not good for the body and have no good result. There is a common saying among the Chinese, "to attain good outcome from any project, one should sharp the tool first." If one is correctly and perfectly applying this statement in martial art training to strengthen the body, one will result with a strong and healthy body and excellent martial art skill. Therefore, if one is solely engaging in martial art training and ignore any cultivation, one should not expect to attain a strong and healthy body with good martial art skill. If one does not know or practice any cultivation, it is not possible to attain good marital art skill and cannot call oneself a martial art practitioner. One should know that cultivating the body is to nourishing the body and training is to applying the body. Since the core of cultivation is to nourishing the body and the core of training is to applying the body, experience practitioners recommended that one should spend 60% of the time is on cultivation exercise and 40% of the time is on training exercise when come to Chinese martial art training. One should know that dynamic is not static, and static is not dynamic. It does not matter how slow the dynamic's motion, it is not static. Although martial art is a type of physical activity. One should adhere to the recommendation of 60% is on the cultivation exercise and 40% is on the training exercise to maintain the body in a strong and healthy condition. It is written in the Yellow Emperor's Internal Medicine Classic, "looking too long hurt the blood; lying down too long hurt the qi; sitting down too long hurt the muscles, standing up too long hurt the bones; walking too long hurt the connective tissues". It requires one should maintain the body in balance during activity. The balance activity emphasizing in Chinese martial art is based on the principle of manipulating the body to become soft so the connective tissues are soft and elasticity, bodily joints are flexible, skins and muscles are firms. If the body is smooth, flexible and nimble, it has versatility, mobility and it is a sign of good health and with many potentials. One is able to act accordingly in martial art engagement.

B. The Objective of Cultivation

1. Introduction

Cultivation is to refining and enhancing the body to attain strong and healthy. This is the final objective. How to begin? What is the method? What is the procedure? Why engage in cultivation? They are not easy to answer. One has to know cultivation is not simply a theory. It is not simply a movement or technique. It has a complete system that have exercising method and profound theory. The exercising method has a specific order. If one is not following the order to practice, it has no benefit but all harmful.

There is a saying that if the heart (mind) has tranquility. It is the road to heaven. If the heart (mind) is lost and fear, it is the road to hell. From this statement, one can see that cultivation should begin with cultivating the heart (mind). If one understood only the good and evil in cultivating the heart (mind), nothing else, it is easy to get lost. Therefore, cultivation begins with to cultivating the heart (mind) as the first step. Obviously, heart (mind) is not referring to the physiologic organ, it is referring to the intangible controller of the mind intention, morality, conscious and other. Cultivation is beginning with how to remove and empty the heart (mind). Lao Tzu written in the Dao De Jing that in its nature state, the heart (mind) is in favor of calm and tranquility. Unfortunately, the heart (mind) is interfered by emotion and temptation, so it is not calm and tranquil. It needs to remove and empty the emotion and temptation so it will become calm and tranquil. Therefore, in order to have calm and tranquil heart (mind), it has to distance itself from emotion and temptation. When one has empty heart (mind), the heart (mind) is calm and tranquil. One is able to concentrate to accumulating qi and when the qi is strong, it fortifies the essence so the body is healthy. Otherwise, if the heart (mind) is not calm and tranquil, always wondering and hesitating, nothing is done.

Although cultivation is an important process to achieve good health. Without the process of cultivating the heart (mind) as a foundation, it is not possible to have any cultivation's success. Daoist Lu Dong Bin in the Tang Dynasty (618-907 AD) said "without a good cultivating the heart (mind) as a foundation, it is not able to distinguish the cultivation path is correct. Therefore, it is not possible to talk about cultivation."

Today, there are many people believed that when one is engaging in meditation to attain tranquility, one is cultivating the heart (mind). The longer one is able to remain in this mind set, it is the skill of cultivating the heart (mind). However, traditional Chinese practitioners believed that the seven emotions (anger, happiness, worry, sadness, sorrow, fear and horror) and the six temptations (wind, cold, heat, humidity, dry and fire) are mainly affected our health. Therefore, traditional method of cultivating the heart (mind) is to managing these seven emotions and six temptations by kept them neutral, not to express themselves outward. The skill is determining by how well one is managing it. It is very different from some of the contemporary practitioners' believed.

When come to the method of cultivating the heart (mind), Daoist Wang Chong Yang (1113-1170) written that one should practice cultivating the heart (mind) during happy time and unhappy time. Therefore, cultivating the heart (mind) should be part of one's daily work project. Traditional practice required that walking, talking, sitting and lying down should not separate from cultivating the heart (mind). If one is separating from this, it is not correct. Therefore, it requires that the practitioner must cultivating the heart (mind) every day and every moment. It does not matter it is during a happy time or an unhappy time, one must cultivate one's heart (mind) to have a happier and healthier life. For this reason, there were many hermits throughout history isolated themselves from society by living alone in remoted areas such as forests and caves to cultivate the heart (mind). Therefore, it is often spoken that skillful and experience hermits are living among people in the crowded cities and unskillful hermits are living in the forests and caves to reduce interaction with other. In addition, we observed Daoist school of teaching offers exercises have the content of cultivating the heart (mind) and body as a foundation exercise. This is often referring to as the component of the fundamental exercise.

The reason why one should cultivate the heart (mind) is to have spiritual concentration and spiritual concentration is for qi accumulation and qi accumulation is to nourish and fortify the essence. It is only when the essence is fortified then the body is strong and healthy. Spirit, qi and essence are the three treasures of the human body. Each one of them is divided into four grades. Spirit has sleepy, murky, clarity and transparent. Qi has short, long, suppress and release; essence has infant, youth, adult and senior. When one is engaging in qi cultivation, keep these elements in mind to formulate a correct exercising method and attain success.

2. Humanity in Harmony

Humanity in harmony with nature is an ancient Chinese philosophical concept concerning the relationship between humanity and nature. It has nothing to do with ruling gods and spirits. It has four aspects of reflecting these relationships: humanity and nature having similar features; humanity and nature being connected to each other; humanity and nature corresponding to each other; and the principles of humanity principles and of nature principles being one. This concept of harmony has had a deep and profound influence on all areas of traditional Chinese culture.

The idea that humanity and nature have similar features means that they were created from the same source, original qi. Based on the idea that humanity and nature are connected to each other was the belief of ancient Chinese philosophers that the myriad things in nature were created by Yin qi and Yang qi. In the relationship between humanity and nature, nature is the big universe; within this big universe, there is a smaller universe, and this smaller universe is called humanity. The Yin qi and the Yang qi of this smaller universe are constantly interacting with the Yin qi and the Yang qi from the bigger universe. Based on the idea that humanity and nature are in a corresponding relationship was the belief of ancient Chinese philosophers that qi circulation in the big universe regularly exchanges information with the qi circulation in the smaller universe. Ancient Chinese philosophers believed that to attain the condition of humanity in harmony with nature, according to the above relationships between humanity and nature, one should research the principles of humanity from the corresponding principles of nature, so that these two sets of principles are together in harmony.

With the understanding of the four relationships described, ancient Chinese conducted themselves based on the following principles, "following the order from nature as basic; taking the virtue as important as soul" in term of cultivation in their daily life. Ancient Chinese practitioners had done by developing the discipline to harnessed the qi from the universe; developing the discipline to accumulated the qi in the body; living the life style followed nature and preserving the qi by conducted in good behavior.

C. Training in Traditional Chinese Martial Art

1. Introduction

Although traditional Chinese martial art has much information, it has two systems (internal and external), many styles, three major training methods in forms, combat simulations and gong exercises, four types of bare hand techniques in grapping, wresting, striking and kicking and five types of weapon techniques in hitting, chopping, cutting, stabbing and thrusting. Although it has many information, it is not separating from its core, cultivation. With the cultivation, the body is stronger and healthier and every technique is supplying with power. Otherwise, it is but calisthenics.

The core of combat is involving the body and its four limbs. It does not matter it is the Chinese external martial art system or the Chinese internal martial art system, it is but Chinese martial art system. Chinese martial art is involving with the body. In the body, the heart (mind) and its creativity are the internal work and the movements from the four limbs are the external work. Internal work is cultivation. It is the process of internal nourishment. External work is training. It is the conditioning and application of the body and its parts. When combine the two together, it yielded amazing result. Therefore, one should keep in mind that the body is the core and the body parts are the application when come to Chinese martial art training. If the core is not good, the application is not good. Application is difficult to achieve and a good, strong and healthy body is even more difficult. When executing a technique, the body has to be well connected. It means when executing a technique, the body is connecting well to the shoulders and arms, and hips and feet. To have a well connection, it means all body parts are permeating with qi so the body is nimble, soft, energize, mobile, agile and flexible in executing a technique. In order for the four limbs to have techniques, the fingers, palms, knees, feet and toes must search for the targets or move accordingly. Although it is said that the technique is manifesting at the four limbs. It is actually from the body, hands and feet. It is the result of top and bottom coordination. The entire body is connecting and applying it together. This unity is called manifesting at the fingers and discharging at the bottom of the feet. This explained the relationship between the body and its parts in application. The body cannot separate from the application and the application is initiating from the body. Training the body and training the four limbs have specific exercises. It does not matter how many time one practices, always pay attention to the body and its parts in each practice. Overall, it is beginning from information to familiarity to wisdom, inside and outside, all have wisdom, and inside and outside, all have harmony. All actions and reactions are based on one's mind intention. Skill is developing from a long term practice. It is only if one narrows the scope of studying the subject than one is able to have better chance to achieve a meaningful and high level skill.

It does not matter a technique is belonging to the internal or external Chinese martial art system, technique is about body manipulation and power. Martial art is about applying the technique. It is about the physical application of the mind intention, body movement, stepping, eye movement and hand movement. In the subject of practice, it is about the application and familiarity of the techniques, and discharging and retreating of power. Cultivation is about body condition and preparation necessary requirement for martial art training. Martial art training is the manifestation of cultivation. To engage in martial art training, one needs a strong and healthy body. Otherwise, it is not possible to attain good martial art skill.

Traditional Chinese martial art is one of the Chinese traditional cultures and heritages. From its function and information, it is not simply a combat art or self-defense art. When manipulating the body parts to move as martial art techniques and forms, it is to demonstrate its performing art, martial art application and health maintenance merits. Traditional Chinese martial art is based on the traditional Chinese culture, Lao Tzu's and Confucius's philosophical teachings as its basic. It has the content of internal and external attributes, martial ethnics, physical and spiritual practices, and it has three major types of technical training in martial art forms, martial art combat simulations and martial art gong exercises. It is truly a unique physical sport and competition program that is different from its peer. As a combat art, it has bare hand forms, weapon forms and partner forms. As a martial art, it is much more complex than this. One cannot simply describe it in a sentence. From its technical training, it has martial art gong exercises training has fundamentals and supplementary exercises, martial art combat simulations training has solo drill and partner drill exercises and connecting the bare hand techniques or weapon techniques together into a routine for the martial art forms training has fast and slow movements. The three types of training to improve body condition and quality as well as technical proficiency in martial art engagement. In addition, the three trainings are interconnected. The function of the gong exercises training is to provide martial art forms training and martial art combat simulations training with preparation. Therefore, martial art forms training and martial art combat simulations training demonstrate the result of gong exercises training. Martial art forms training provides martial art combat simulations training with versatile, swift, coordination and spontaneous actions and reactions. Martial art combat simulations training can elevate one's consciousness of a martial art's offense and defense—the understanding of each individual technique's offensive and defensive values. This consciousness enhances greatly the forms' martial art merit. The results and benefits of these three types of traditional Chinese martial art trainings are not to be found in other sports.

2. Traditional Chinese Martial Art Training

Although there are three major types of training, one summarized the training in the traditional Chinese martial art into the following: They are the striking power, speed, response and offense/defense techniques and curriculum. As long as one possessed the superior skill and abilities of these elements, one possessed combat skill and ability with the practical function such as self-defense, amusement, health maintenance, personal development, and tempering the heart (mind) and soul, etc. Due to the training of these abilities by different method and transmission, traditional Chinese martial art developed into many styles. A practitioner's skill is not determining by a specific style. It is based on how well a practitioner process, dedicate and devote in the method of training and adhere to the requirement from a specific style. This is similar to hiking. There are many routes can climate to the summit. Which route is danger? Which route is easier and which route is difficult? Which route is shorter and which route is longer? Among many routes available, one should choose a route that is better for oneself. The answer is obviously the same with martial art training. A student should choose a style that fit his/her body condition, personality, temperament and requirement. However, to develop the elements mentioned, different style has different training method and requirement to develop the elements. It is not possible for one to agree with all of the training methods. Therefore, there is difference in skill one developed.

a. Striking Power

Martial art power and daily activity power are two separate things. In physic, we understood power is the product of weight multiple acceleration. In other word, the bigger the fist, the quicker the speed and longer the distance, the acceleration increase and the striking power increase. Therefore, when come to delivering power, we witness many people usually retreated the arm to create more distance from the target before strike. This action increases acceleration to produce greater striking power.

Traditional Chinese martial art often discussed the object of power as striking power and generating power. This is different from western sport activity due to their difference in application and training method. Of cause, there is no doubt that sport power training method maybe developed quicker result. It is mainly relying on physical built. However, physically stronger is no guarantee to cause more devastation in combat situation.

When one launches a strike in combat situation, is the striking power increase or decrease? When the strike land on the opponent, is the opponent neutralizes the striking power or fully absorb it? Is the striking target on the muscle, bone or other part of the body? All of these need answer and solution. The answer come from gong exercises training.

Obviously, take a shorter route and produce greater amount of striking power is the best solution to the questions from above. To achieve this objective, there are many training methods in traditional Chinese martial art. Therefore, it does not matter that the training is on the form, solo drill, partner drill, partner form, weapon form and gong exercises training. All are involving with power in some degree. What is important is the gong exercise training provide from a specific style. Therefore, all styles of Chinese martial art are always looking out for a better and effective training method and exercise.

b. Speed

All effective martial art strikes require speed, the faster, the better. I am sure there are many people would ask, Tai Chi Chuan does not require. All the movements are done so slow. How can its' techniques are striking effectively? One should know that the slowness in Tai Chi Chuan practice is but a method of training. It is not for practical application. It is only under slowness condition that one is fully understand all the requirements in Tai Chi Chuan such as relaxation, concentration, coordination and integration, etc. To most of the people, it is difficult to understand these requirements when a movement is done quickly. Therefore, one has to slow down to practice the movements in Tai Chi Chuan. Of cause, this slowness training method has many more functions such as applying the mind intention, and improving the quality of the connective tissues, bones and body integration as I discussed. There is a saying among the Tai Chi Chuan practitioners, slow speed training is for fundamental training and fast speed training is for application training. Tai Chi Chuan is employing the tactic of "slowness to defeat fast and preferred to strike second, not first to defeat first". How can one attain this result? The answer is depending on the distance and skill. The Tai Chi Chuan classics said, "when the opponent moves fast, I react quickly. When the opponent moves slowly, I response slowly." Martial art is an unpredictable activity. The result is based on one's preparation and training.

As I mentioned before, it is common practice when come to delivering power, one would retreat the arm to create a longer distance then punch forward. The greater the distance, the acceleration is greater and the arm travels forward produced more velocity. Tai Chi Chuan does not need to retreat the arm to deliver the power. The power is delivered directly from the contact area with the muscles are relaxed. This is the result of body integration. The integral power is generating from the connective tissues and bones. There is no tension or movement among the muscles. Practitioners called this striking power as internal power because when the power is delivering, there is little or no muscle movement. Experience Tai Chi Chuan practitioners called this skill as the small circle or no circle skill.

c. Response

If the response is not fast, it is useless, even if one has a powerful striking power. If one does not able to avoid the oncoming strike and not able to siege the opportunity to counter strike when the opponent exposes all the weakness. Without proper solution, how can one victory from the confrontation.

There are many ways to train for response in traditional Chinese martial art. Traditionally, the training is happening after the form training. Today, there are many practitioners do not understand the form training objective. They interpreted performing the form as gymnastic performance and always practice it as a complete form each time. Therefore, there are many practitioners believed that learning and training the form is the martial art training. Traditionally, after a student learned a form, the teacher would breakdown a form to its individual movement and explain the offense/defense values from each movement. This training is called assimilation. A student would practice these individual techniques as a solo drill training to better understand their practical value. Next, a student would practice the same techniques with a partner to better understand and aware their offense/defense technical value and how it is operating in engagement. Usually, the partner is the teacher first and later with a classmate. This is called partner drill training. From this training, one acquires the response, speed ability, familiarity and operation of the techniques. Therefore, traditional Chinese martial art response and speed abilities came from form training. Unfortunately, there are many practitioners today do not fully understand and or misinterpreted its true objective of solo form, partner form, weapon form, solo drill and partner drill trainings today. They assumed them as the physical programs demonstrations and performances.

d. Offensive and Defense Techniques

i. Introduction

The character and personality of each martial art practitioner are different. There are some practitioners highly educated and intelligent; there are some have strong will and perseverance; there are some very quiet and other outspoken. With different personality among practitioners, their actions are different. This goes with the launching of martial art techniques and tactics. One should expect some techniques are powerful while others are soft; some technique maybe fast and other slow. One maybe good with offense and the second person maybe good with defense, no matter, one should expect the opponent's action have multiple dimensions. One must prepare well.

Chinese martial art techniques are the bodily movements developed from martial engagement properly execute on to the opponent's body. The principles of martial art techniques are the common rules applying among different styles of Chinese martial art. The rules reflected the feature of Chinese culture and martial art style such as the unique application of power, practice, the accuracy of the technical employment and the method of training. Therefore, these rules formed the specific style among Chinese martial art multiple styles. If a style is against these rules, it is not considered as a Chinese martial art style. If a style lost its feature, it would have lost its distinctive feature as a specific Chinese martial art style as well. Therefore, one sees the rules as the general guideline for Chinese martial art and specific style, and one should understand that the same rules are not always applying in all the styles of Chinese martial art. One has to understand that when the rules are modified and changed according to the changed of the objectives, practitioners and marital confrontational situations, the rules would have to changed accordingly.

The martial art techniques are the best offensive and defensive movements from a martial art form. Form is a collection of techniques connected together. It is function as a warehouse for the techniques so one would not forget in transmission. Techniques are the bodily movements elevated to become practical martial art movements that have technical merit. When the bodily movements became permanent as the martial art techniques, they are followed the offensive and defensive martial art principles and they have combat technical value and function. They are from bodily movements elevated into martial art practical techniques applying in combat situation. This demonstrated that combat situation is the stage for martial art techniques' technical application and motivation of their development. Therefore, a good form requires many generations and practitioners experience. If a technique is not applying in combat situation, soon or later, the technique's technical value is no longer have any significant value in combat function intended. This mean that although one applied the body to move according to the technical intention, however, the technical movement is not able to function as combat situation requirement. It is not a martial art technique but simply as a bodily movement.

It is only when one is incorporating the combat situation in applying the techniques in practice than one is better and correctly studying and mastering the techniques' intended function and value. Executing the martial art techniques is reflecting and demonstrating their engagement values and principles. When one recognizes these principles, one is able to freely applying the techniques during martial art engagement without any pre-programming set in. One is truly attained high level martial art skill.

The training and application in Chinese martial art, in theory, they are following nature internally and following the feature and anatomy of the physiologic organs externally. They are very practical and efficient by involving and coordinating the entire body in each technique. The ability, execution and accomplishment of the offensive and defensive techniques are done by demonstrating, associating and incorporating with the physiologic organs and their functions. The amazing offensive and defensive transformation are often revealing the internal attributes involvement. Therefore, martial art applications and trainings are complementing each other. The two are so close that there are some styles treated training is the same as application.

The application of the defensive and offensive techniques is highly emphasizing on the combination of spirit, mind intention, power and physical movement. The combination produced devastation result. The physical movement has pre-requisite substantial and insubstantial differentiation so that one is able to applying the body as soft, quickly and freely as there is no bone. The offensive and defensive transformations are following the rules of circulating is to yielding and straightness is to discharging. This is the same as soft power is to yielding and hard power is to discharging and finally, martial art tactical transformations and applications are based on the opponent's action. In order to attain this spontaneous response in engagement, beside the body has to be soft as it has no bone, the body has to position upright like a scale, so the waist moves freely as a cartwheel. In other word, it is necessary for the body to have equilibrium condition at all time, so the body has mobility and versatility. When one is able to positioning the body in this way, all the offensive and defensive techniques are employing naturally, quickly and freely. Every technique has profundity, and every execution is demonstrating skill and power.

In term of performing the profound application techniques, it is often described in the following statements. "Striking hand is invisible. If one witnesses the hand, the skill is not very high", "Hitting hand is invisible. When one witnesses the hand, the hitting is already there". These statements explained the role of power and speed in martial art and the relationship between visible techniques and invisible techniques and "flowering strike for showmanship is covering a great space and genuine strike is happening in a straight line". From this statement, it explained further the relationship between the fake and genuine strikes. A visible strike is obvious and it is easily neutralizing by the opponent. Therefore, most of the victory is won by the invisible technique.

ii. The Nature of Martial Art Techniques

Martial art techniques are the vehicle to physically demonstrating, reflecting and reviewing martial art objective and intention through bodily movement. Each bodily movement has offensive and defensive values. If one is always taking the position on defense, it is difficult to win any engagement. On the other hand, if one is solely on the offense, it is difficult to win as well. However, if one applies both offensive and defensive strategies, the chance of winning is higher. The offensive and defensive techniques are based on the feature and nature of bodily movements functions.

We know that any martial art technique cannot be separate from bodily movement function and human anatomy. The anatomic structure of a human body is similar to a cross. The center crossing area is the location of the body's vital organs and the weakness part of the body. Therefore, it is the most important areas for the offense to attack and the defense to protect. The bodily movement function as technique to attack in martial art engagement is not solely referring to the movement generated from the hands. It can be from the head, shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees and feet. These seven bodily parts arsenals known as the seven stars. The defensive movement is not only applying the seven parts of the body mentioned to defense the attack. One can move the body and with feet. Martial art techniques are often executing with offensive and defensive values at the same time to balance and protect. Every movement is well coordinated with stepping to get close to or away from the opponent. Anyway, any effective martial art technique must manifest at the body parts, relying on the quality and condition of the body and the principle of the body mechanic. Otherwise, it is not a good technique and not effective. Therefore, to improve the body condition is one of the fundamental trainings in Chinese martial art and the quality body condition is a skill acquiring from gong exercises training. All of these require a knowledgeable teacher.

iii. The Formation of Martial Art Techniques

Martial art technique is a technical bodily movement capable to make contact with the opponent in martial engagement as discussed. It is divided into a dynamic technique and static technique. When we observe the tract of a bodily motion from point A to point B, this is called dynamic technique. However, when we observe the body part positioning only at point A or B without any bodily motion, this is called static technique or posture. To distinguish the two, experience practitioners often say that dynamic condition is the soul of martial art and static posture is its shell. We know that to make any contact with the opponent, one has to move. A bodily movement is called martial art technique when a movement is able to make contact with the opponent. Martial art technique is the technical demonstration of bodily movement with a martial art intention or objective. The objective is often done by seven areas of the body. The technical intention has offensive and defensive values. Therefore, due to its feature, dynamic technique is the soul of martial art activity and posture is its foundation. Therefore, in order to have quality skill, one must improve the foundation. In the history of Chinese martial art, the techniques originally deployed simply to function to defense oneself. This is the natural responses without any conscious effort and meaning. Later, these simple responses developed into conscious effort that have offensive and defensive values. On the offensive responses, the movements were not always accurate and powerful. On the defensive response, the movements were not always effective. One wasted a lot of energy and not properly mobilized the body's natural resource. After many years and many generations' involvement of practices, experiences and evaluations, there were many good and effective techniques developed with unique feature, principle, function and training method shared among practitioners. This is the development of a specific Chinese martial art style. Martial art techniques were developed from basic natural behavioral responses. Later, these natural behavioral responses became the best offensive and defensive values practical martial techniques. They were the techniques employed with minimum amount of effort to yielded the best result. Due to the necessary employment in offense and defense unpredictable situations, a collection of these valuable offensive and defensive martial techniques come together to forming a series of connected techniques called "form" functions for the practitioners not to forget in transmission from generation to generation. This unique way of transmission one only found in Chinese martial art. Although any bodily movement is called martial art technique today, traditionally, a martial art technique is referring to the bodily movement which capable to make contact with the opponent. Otherwise, it is simply called bodily movement.

iv. Seven Stars

The creation of the Chinese martial art techniques is the result of forbears' practical experiences. Although the Chinese martial art has many styles and techniques, they are but the functions and applications of the 14 major parts of the body. They are head, two shoulders, two elbows, two hands, two hips, two knees, two feet and buttock. Therefore, understanding the anatomy function and usage and fine tune these body parts well will contribute a great deal in executing the martial art techniques properly and effectively.

* Head

Head is the most important part of the body. When the head moves, the entire body moves accordingly. Therefore, the head is possessing the best integrative power. In order to applying the head to strike correctly, the head moves according to the feet stepping, the hands must to block to create an opening and the body is maintaining balance by not over-extend from the front leg or leaning too much to either side of the body. If the body is not positioning up right, it has no balance, no bodily integration and no integrative power. It is difficult to move. Therefore, it is said that the head strike picks the target is based on the feet movement and one must advance forward toward the target quickly in order to be effective.

Head strike is often applying five areas of the head. They are the top, front, back, and left and right sides. Since the head is possessing the best integrative power, it can cause great devastation. When executing a head strike, the neck should be stretched, the back should be straight, so the power generating from the back leg travels to the top of the head and the hands are preparing to block to create a target for the head to strike.

* Two Shoulders

The shoulders are the root section of the upper body. It is often applying by leaning toward the opponent. When applying the shoulders to strike, the arms are generally positioning down to the rib cages to protect the ribs. When advancing the body to get closer to the opponent to strike, one foot is often positioning in between the opponent's feet.

The shoulders strike is often picking the chest as the target. It strikes with one side of the shoulder then following with the other side of the shoulder, in left or right, and front or back motions combination. Some time, one is applying the same shoulder to strike left and right, top and bottom targets. There is a common expression that goes like this, "Shoulder strikes is not separating from the elbows. The elbows strike is not separating from the hands" to explain their unique combination strike.

When one is applying the shoulders strike, experience practitioners often said that one must get closer to the opponent. Otherwise, it does not work.

* Two Elbows

Elbows are very important part of the body applying as martial art weapons. They are so because the elbows are the middle section of the upper body and the control center of the arms' movements. When the elbow bends, it becomes a short and powerful weapon that is difficult to stop. People often said that they are preferring to strike 10 times by the hands rather than one time by the elbows. It is so because elbows strike is powerful and travel in short distance. It is difficult to block. They have fatal consequence.

If one has a loosen waist, one is applying the elbows easily. Therefore, loosen the waist is one of the fundamental exercises. When an elbow bent, it has the techniques of applying the arm to yield, to press down, to move forward to intercept and to strike with the tip. It is possible for the elbow tip to produce motions to strike in many directions as well such as move up, down, left and right directions. There is a common statement that said, "The elbows are striking in four directions."

* Two Hands

The hands are the head section of the upper body. They can use as long-range weapon to strike. One can quickly change the hand into fist to strike or open the fist into the palm to strike or with the fingers to stab. It is a very practical weapon. Hands strike has many options. It begins with the hands, follow with the elbows and finally, end with the shoulders. If the hand strikes blocked, one bends the arm and strike with the elbow. If the elbow strikes blocked, one quickly lean forward with the shoulder strikes or chest strikes. One can see, the hands and arms can deliver many strikes and variations in a short time. When the hands strike, there are supporting from the elbows and shoulders. When applying the elbows or shoulders to strike, the hands are functioning to create an opening target. The three sections (hand, elbow and shoulder) are often acting as one unit.

* Two Hips

The hips are the root section of the lower body. The muscle groups are thick and big, and the bones are big as well so it can generate a large amount of power and not get hurt so easily in collision. The hips are divided into left and right, each hip is divided into inside and outside. When applying the hips to strike, it is necessary to move the feet. Since the mobility and flexibility on the hips are limited, they are emphasizing mainly move in left and right directions and sink downward. Hip strikes mainly pick the target of the opponent's middle section and sometime, the lower section.

* Two Knees

The knees are the middle section of the lower body. Although the range of motion is not as large as the feet and hands, the intensity to cause harm from the knees are very great. The knees have many striking techniques. They are often picked the middle and lower body of the opponent as target.

In order to execute the technique properly, one has to move the body and the coordination from the hands and feet. There is a common statement saying, "applying the feet to kick in a long range strike and a closer distance with the knees."

There are many ways to applying the knees to strike: One can lift the knees up to strike to the chest, face and groin. Bend the knees to have downward stump. Spin the body to have the knees strike to either left or right sides, and finally, applying the hands to intercept the opponent's strike and following with the knees strike, etc.

* Two Feet

The feet are the head section of the lower body, and it is also the root section of the entire body. One can observe it is often coordinating with the hands to strike. The feet serve two functions in martial art activity. It is a supporting center for body balance as well as a striking weapon. Therefore, it utilizes more than the hands. There is a common statement said, "The feet strike 70% and the hands are 30%."

One can apply the feet to strike in many ways: Applying the toes to kick, the heel to kick, ankle and the top of the feet to hook in outward and inward motions and applying the bottom of the foot to have downward stump, etc.

* Buttock

The buttock is referring to the coccyx. Since its movement is very limited. It is very uncommon applying it as martial art weapon. The most common techniques are turning the body to the left, right and shaking the body. In addition, there are two techniques some people used. They are sinking and bending the body. Sinking the body is to maintaining the body in balance and bending the body is to applying the body to performing an over the head throw technique to put the opponent to the ground.

e. Curriculum

Traditional Chinese martial art developed into many styles and each style has its own distinctive feature, requirement and training program. Since each style has its own system of training program, beginning students find this is difficult to choose among them. To excel, one has to seek out a style that fit his/her body condition, personality and temperament. Beginning students often asked what is the curriculum? What program to learn first? And what program to learn last? Traditional Chinese martial art as a complete system, generally, it begins with fundamentals, fundamental gong exercise, solo form, solo drill, partner drill, partner form, weapon form, weapon partner form, supplementary gong exercise and sparring. Each program is preparing for the next program. One should not skip any. It takes time and effort to attain any success.

i. Fundamental

Chinese martial art has many styles and training programs. This is difficult for the beginning students to choose and to study. Although there are many, due to the fact that fundamentals are the same among different styles of Chinese martial art. They are easy to learn, practice and remember. Therefore, a beginning student should and must begin with the fundamentals. As long as one is regularly practice the fundamentals, one is preparing the body. This is like building a skyscraper. It is beginning with a good and strong foundation.

Fundamentals are referring to the training of simple and common movements. It included positioning of the body and body parts, and movements of the hands, eyes, body position, stance, stepping and waist rotation, etc. It is often said that when one executes a hand technique without moving the feet, one is looking for trouble. In executing a movement, if the head is looking down like a dog and the body is stretching like a cat, one's skill is very poor. Therefore, one must spend time to practice these basic and simple fundamentals. If one cannot master these basic, it is not possible to attain quality skill.

ii. Fundamental Gong Exercise

Fundamental gong exercise is referring to the exercise to improve the quality of the body condition such as flexibility, agility, strengthen, endurance, coordination, balance and resilience, etc. It has an objective of to improve the body condition, technical performance and efficiency. Therefore, martial art fundamental gong exercises training is a training for the beginning students to build foundation. It is a guarantee for martial art performance, physical health and technical improvement. It is also an effective method of physical injury prevention. Therefore, it is not solely for the beginning students but all students. Therefore, to achieve quality skill, one must spend time to work on the fundamental gong exercise regularly.

iii. Form

Form is a routine connected all the basic bodily movements or techniques together. Therefore, a form is a collection of individual techniques connected together with a specific objective, Training, learning and practicing the form from a specific style is by following the order of the movements, principles and requirements to mold the body according to each style as a method to improve the body condition, coordination and technique. It is involving with three steps. They are: learning the techniques, principles and requirements, applying the techniques, principles and requirements and refining the techniques, principles and requirements. Therefore, form is a good entry level for martial art training. In addition, form is function as a warehouse of techniques to keep them together so one would not forget them. A good form is the product of many generations' experiences and efforts.

iv. Solo Drill

It is referring to a method of training by practicing the individual technique derived from the form. It is a method of training to improve one's body condition, technique, timing, versatility, resilience, sensitivity, power delivery and coordination, etc. The information is based on a knowledgeable teacher, not a famous teacher.

v. Partner Drill

It is referring to a method of training involving two or more practitioners to practice the same technique from the solo drill training to improve one's martial art awareness and combat skill. Through the training, one is better applying the individual technique in combat situation. To some people, the operation serves as an introduction to the studying of martial art offensive/defensive operation.

vi. Partner Form

It is referring to the method of training extent from the partner drill. This method of training is practicing the routine (form) comes from connecting all the partner drill exercises together, so the drill exercises would not get lost in transmission. It has the same function as partner drill.

vii. Weapon

Studying bare hand form and weapon form are basically the same. It is different but with the hand holding a weapon. Therefore, weapon is but the extension of the arm. Through weapon training, practitioner has a better understanding about martial art offense/defense knowledge. Although weapon form is developed from bare hand form, there is difference in training content. The fundamental training is much more difficult to perform in weapon and each weapon has its unique fundamental requirement. In practice, the body, body parts and weapon are coordinating and moving together, so they are moving in unity such as the hands, eyes, body and stepping are unified, upper and lower body parts have coordination, and inside and outside attributes have harmony. Otherwise, one may harm himself/herself in training and practicing.

There are many weapons available and each weapon has its special unique feature, function, value, requirement and technique. Long weapon has its unique feature and value. Short weapon has its feature and unique value. Soft weapon has its feature and unique value. The objective of practicing weapon is to have a better understanding the martial art offense/defense technical ability, awareness and function. Therefore, partner weapon form is much more difficult to perform then the bare hand partner form.

viii. Supplementary Gong Exercise

Martial art is about surviving from life and death situations. Therefore, there is no such thing as over preparing, practitioner always open and pursue for new and effective method to better prepare oneself. Supplementary gong exercise is referring to the additional exercise with the objective on application and power to improve the offense and defense technical proficiency.

Although the fundamental gong exercise and supplementary exercise shared similar function in improving the fundamentals and body condition such as balance, strengthen, flexibility, agility, endurance and resilience, etc., however, the difference between them is that the supplementary gong exercise is physically more challenge.

Let's talk about the difference between fundamentals, application and skill in a martial art. It is similar to the difference in Chinese calligraphy between the structure and arrangement of character strokes. The quality and type of stroke determine the quality of the calligraphy. The composition and arrangement determine the quality of the entire product. Unless each individual stroke possesses quality, one cannot produce quality calligraphy. If one has good quality strokes, but the composition is not good, the final product is not good. On the other hand, if one has good quality strokes and excellent composition, but is writing on poor quality paper and the characters themselves are not interesting, the calligraphy's final product will look dull, confusing, and without any life.

The same is true for a martial art: if one has excellent fundamentals and good techniques, one's skill will be excellent. Fundamentals and skill are similar to composition and arrangement in calligraphy. When it is time to execute the strike, there are multiple applications and variations available. Therefore, one can see that fundamental training plays a very significant role in martial art training and skill development; it is the building block for good martial art skill. Therefore, throughout history, Chinese martial art practitioners always said that if one engages in martial art training without the gong exercise program, it is but a waste of time.

ix. Sparring

Mastering the offense/defense ability is the major objective of martial art training. When one is going through the above training programs, practitioner mastered most of the martial art training content. One has the foundation for sparring, a spontaneous action and reaction training.

How to attain high level martial art skill? It is the awareness and objective for all martial art practitioners. It requires one to correctly and properly train with dedication, devotion, perseverance, confidence and diligence. In other word, one must give it with 100% effort without any hesitation.

Sparring and partner form are very different method of training. Sparring is not a pre-arrangement as in partner form, so it is solely based on one's ability and skill developed from the above list of training programs. Therefore, the sparring method of training is very difficult. Through the training to improve the body condition, mobility, agility, endurance, timing, power discharging, adjustment, mental toughness, intelligence and versatility, most importantly, it is to better mastering the offense/defense techniques, skill and tactics.

3. Conclusion

Although Chinese martial art has three major methods of training in forms, combat simulations and gong exercises. The core of the training is power. The power in Chinese martial art is developing from the connective tissues and bones, not muscles alone. Therefore, an important part of the traditional Chinese martial art training is to developing and refining the body as there is no bone, so that one is able to react to the opponent's strikes accordingly. To has a soft body, it is not an easy task. One has to go through a harsh process of training. It is not for everyone.

As a Chinese martial art practitioner, one should know what is involving in traditional Chinese martial art training. It is the three major trainings in forms, combat simulations and gong exercises. The objective is to developing a curriculum to train the striking power, response, speed and offense/defense techniques necessary to victory, health is but its byproduct. Although the training is harsh, the training is successful if one is clearly understood the objective and committed to the training with dedication, perseverance, devotion, diligence and humble.

D. Conclusion

Traditional Chinese culture is based on following nature order and focusing on the quality of one's virtue (it involves with the subjects of sincerity, loyal, filial act, benevolence, friendship, ritual, intelligence and trustworthy) as soul. With the development of science and technology and with social progress, people's focusing and emphasizing have been veering toward commercialism and personal interest. With this trend, Chinese martial art, as well as many other aspects of traditional Chinese culture, has been transformed. In the name of safety, science, civility, and health, the meaning, objective, values, and training methods of Chinese martial art have undergone changed.

Traditional Chinese martial art is a vigorous and highly competitive physical activity. It is difficult to perform with a victory outcome. Therefore, without a calm and tranquil heart (mind) as a foundation to prepare oneself, it is difficult to have the dedication, confidence, devotion, diligence and perseverance to the harsh training and achieve result. Imagine this, if one is in a highly competitive engagement, the blood rush to the head quickly; one is short and out of breath that felt like the physical organ heart will come out from the chest at any moment. Under this situation, there is no time to think about what tactics to deploy and how to apply the appropriate techniques and skill developed from years of harsh training. Therefore, it is necessary to engage the body in cultivating the heart (mind) to improve the mental and physical conditions and temperament accordingly in martial art affair.

To have a calm and tranquil heart (mind) set is very important in martial art activity, without it, the heart (mind) is searching and wondering all the time. There is no concentration. Without any concentration, it is difficult to accomplish anything. There were many people spend their whole lifetime working on this calm and tranquil heart (mind) and accomplished a whole range of benefits. The benefit is as small as personal performance, character development, family harmony and as big as country establishment, stability and peacefulness. Although the benefit is great, due to its influenced from emotion and temptation, it is difficult to attain calm and tranquil heart (mind) for everyone. Throughout Chinese history, there were many people provided their experiences and practical recommendations to pursuit this subject. Lao Tzu written in the Dao De Jing that in order to have a calm and tranquil heart (mind), one must distance from emotion and temptation. Confucius outline the six steps (halt, standstill, tranquility, peace, ponding and solution) of learning described in his book, The Great Learning. In order to have a calm and tranquil heart (mind), one must begin with to halt oneself from all activities. In regress to managing emotion and temptation, there were many Daoist priests recommended that one should not express the emotion and temptation outward at any time and Wang Chung Yang in the Song Dynasty written that one should practice this management in good time and bad time. To observed this recommendation, there were many hermits isolated themselves from society by living alone in remote areas such as forests and caves to cultivate their hearts (mind). Therefore, it is often spoken that skillful and experience hermits are living among people in the crowded cities and unskillful hermits are living in the forests and caves to reduce their interactions with other.

Although it is no longer observed by many contemporary practitioners, traditional Chinese martial art training begins with the program called Zhan Zhuang (standing pole) to calm and tranquil the heart (mind). It is an exercise to halt oneself from any physical movement so that one is concentrating on the mental condition and comprehending all the transformations are happening inside the body. It is an excellent exercise to develop tranquility and peaceful skill. In the Yellow Emperor's Internal Classic, the Zhan Zhuang training program was described as "It is a method utilized the heaven and earth; mastered the Yin and Yang; inhaled the essential qi; stalled and concentrated on the spirit; integrated the body as one, therefore, attained longevity." In addition, it is an effective method to screening out the disqualify students. Martial art has harsh training preparation. It is not for everyone Therefore, to attain any success in any project, calm and tranquil the heart (mind) is a prerequisite. When one has calm and tranquil heart (mind), the qi is accumulating, essence is fortified and one is able to comprehend all the transformations are happening inside the body.

With the Zhan Zhuang exercise in traditional Chinese static martial art training, the heart (mind) is calm and tranquil, the body is relaxed and qi accumulated from concentration and tranquility. One has patience, dedication, perseverance and confidence results. This method of training is guiding by the principle of pursuing dynamic state from static state. It is better understood as halt any physical movement so one is better to comprehend all the transformations are happening inside the body. With regular practice, calm and tranquility become an ordinary even and the heart (mind) has peace. One has achieved calm and tranquil heart (mind) skill. One is really to engage in the next step of dynamic martial art training. The training begins with to manipulating the body to move according to the practitioner's intention. It means one begins to execute and deliver the profound and powerful techniques with a calm and tranquil mindset. This method of training is guiding by the principle of pursing static state from dynamic state. It is better understood as applying the body to improve the mental condition. Therefore, a complete style of Chinese martial art training is involving the body going through two methods of static and dynamic state trainings. They have the content from cultivation and training.

Chinese martial art is one of the many brilliant heritages of Chinese culture. It is a very complex art and has a large body of vast information. A complete system or style generally has three major areas of technical training—forms training, combat simulations training, and gong (supplementary exercises and fundamental exercises) training—as well as a long transmission lineage and profound philosophical concepts underlying the system's creation and development. The curriculum of a complete system or style is composed of fundamental gong exercises, bare hand forms, weapons forms, partner forms, and supplementary gong exercises to develop skill and power. A Chinese martial art is the product of thousands of years of Chinese anthropology, Chinese culture, social study, and life science and natural science research and development. It has a strong relationship to ancient philosophy, performing art, morality, military warfare, and traditional Chinese medicine and religion.
